We can create a malicious binary, place it in a controlled directory, and prepend that directory to PATH to achieve root command execution.

step_pairs.previous_step_explanation: We need to: 1) locate the vulnerable /opt/netdata/usr/libexec/netdata/plugins.d/ndsudo binary, 2) create a malicious C program that mimics an expected utility (like nvme), 3) compile and place it in /dev/shm, 4) modify PATH to prioritize /dev/shm, 5) execute ndsudo to trigger our malicious binary as root.
step_pairs.previous_step_result: CVE-2024-32019 identified affecting NetData's ndsudo utility. Vulnerable binary is root-owned with SUID bit. Search paths from PATH environment variable allow privilege escalation through PATH injection.
step_pairs.previous_mcp_tasks: Interactive CLI: Locate ndsudo at /opt/netdata/usr/libexec/netdata/plugins.d/ndsudo. Execute PATH=/dev/shm:$PATH /opt/netdata/usr/libexec/netdata/plugins.d/ndsudo nvme-list to trigger exploit.
